parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. GRAMMAR CHECK: Review your draft for these common errors: subject-verb agreement, correct tense (mostly present tense for facts), citation format.
2. STRUCTURE CHECK: Count sentences in each section. Introduction: 5-7? Body paragraphs: 4-6 each? Conclusion: 5-7? If any section is too short, what can you add?
3. MATH SPIRAL: Statistics check. Find all numbers/percentages in your draft. Verify each one against your original source. Change any that are inaccurate.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Your first draft is the most important step in writing. It is NOT meant to be perfect. A first draft is a complete version of your ideas that you will later improve through revision.
content: 📖 Your first draft is the most important step in writing. It is NOT meant to be perfect. A first draft is a complete version of your ideas that you will later improve through revision.

Today, you will share your first draft with a partner for PEER REVIEW. Your partner will read your report and give you feedback using a structured checklist. Good peer review is not just about finding mistakes — it is about helping the writer see their work from a new perspective.

As a reviewer, your job is to be honest but KIND. Focus on the BIG PICTURE first: Is the argument clear? Is the structure logical? Is the evidence strong? Only then move to smaller issues like grammar and vocabulary.

As a writer receiving feedback, your job is to LISTEN and CONSIDER. You do not have to accept all feedback, but you must think about it carefully and decide which suggestions will truly improve your report.
